ingredients.name: Jackfruit seeds (kos ata)
ingredients.notes: seeds from a ripe jackfruit; or separately purchased. The white outer fibrous skin must be removed after boiling -- the inner seed is the edible part.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: 1 cup, for initial boiling of the seeds

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.notes: juiced; optional, added at the end

steps.instruction: If using fresh jackfruit seeds, first boil them in salted water for 15-20 minutes until just tender. Drain and, once cool enough to handle, peel off the thin white fibrous outer skin from each seed -- the brown inner seed coat is edible and does not need removal. Cut each seed in half or leave whole.

Heat the coconut oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add the curry leaves, pandan leaf, onion, garlic, and green chillies. Saute until the onion softens, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the turmeric, chilli powder, and curry powder. Stir briefly to coat the aromatics.
Add the pre-boiled jackfruit seeds and salt. Toss well in the spice base.
Pour in the thin coconut milk. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 10-12 minutes until the seeds are fully tender and the flavours have infused.
Pour in the thick coconut milk. Simmer uncovered for 3-5 minutes on low heat until the gravy thickens. Stir in the lime juice if using. Taste and adjust salt.
Serve hot with rice. Jak seed curry has a pleasantly nutty, starchy flavour -- it pairs well alongside a lighter vegetable dish to balance its richness.

collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 5+ independent sources; moderate trust score reflects fewer available English-language sources compared to more mainstream Sri Lankan curries
notes: Jackfruit seeds (kos ata) are a by-product of eating ripe jackfruit and are treated as a prized vegetable in Sri Lankan cooking rather than discarded. Fresh seeds must be pre-boiled before currying since they are hard and starchy when raw; the thin white outer fibrous skin is slightly bitter when cooked and is typically peeled off after boiling (the brown inner seed coat is fine to eat). The flavour of jak seed curry is reminiscent of chestnuts or very starchy potato -- mild and slightly nutty. Seeds from the same jackfruit as the young jackfruit curry (sl_019 polos) are different -- ripe jackfruit seeds are larger and more starchy. Some cooks also roast the boiled seeds before currying for a deeper, nuttier flavour. Canned jackfruit seeds in brine are available in some Asian grocers and eliminate the boiling step.
